reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and findNonWeekend in shared/schedules.ts and has the server's daily-skip checks call the new shared predicate instead of d.isWeekend.

duplication.why: The off-day test is defined once (isOffDay) and the template's two identical adjustment ternaries are folded into one local closure; only the holidays argument is threaded through each caller.

placement.why: The holiday rule sits with the weekend rule in shared/schedules.ts, the field is added to RecurConfig and to parseRecurDate's schedule data, and callers only pass it along.

scope.why: Focused on the feature; the small restructuring of createScheduleList into an `adjust` closure and the widened scan margin in getDatesInRange are related but go a bit beyond the minimum.

maintainability.why: A single predicate and a stepping loop are easy to own, though exporting it under an alias (`export { isOffDay as isWeekendOrHoliday }`) and a margin of `3 + holidays.length` are slightly ad hoc.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every weekend check (getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, getNextDate/findNonWeekend, getDateWithSkippedWeekend, createScheduleList) now goes through isOffDay/getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the template's previously duplicated ternaries are merged rather than reshaped.

one_place.where: isOffDay in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts (exported as isWeekendOrHoliday), used by getDateWithSkippedWeekend, findNonWeekend and the daily-skip branches in server/schedules/app.ts.
